root_cause.text: The dirty clusters counter was decremented in two different code paths during block allocation failure—once in `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` when `ext4_handle_dirty_metadata()` fails, and again in `ext4_mb_new_blocks()` in the error handling path, causing a double decrement.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "the former decrements both cluster counters and returns the error up to ext4_mb_new_blocks(). The latter falls into the !ar->len out path which decrements the dirty clusters counter a second time, creating the inconsistency." The patch resolves this by removing the `percpu_counter_sub(&sbi->s_dirtyclusters_counter, reserv_clstrs)` call from `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` and consolidating all dirty cluster counter decrements into a single location in `ext4_mb_new_blocks()` at the `out:` label, ensuring the counter is only decremented once regardless of success or failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove incorrect dirty cluster counter decrement that was causing accounting inconsistency in non-delalloc block allocations.
intent_record.what: Removed a conditional block that subtracted reserved clusters from the dirty clusters counter when the EXT4_MB_DELALLOC_RESERVED flag was not set in ac->ac_flags.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the decrement of s_dirtyclusters_counter for non-delalloc allocations. Previously, when allocating disk space without the delalloc flag, the code would reduce the dirty cluster count by the reserved cluster amount. Now this reduction no longer occurs, meaning dirty cluster accounting will not be decremented in this code path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused parameter from ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() function call to simplify the interface.
intent_record.what: Removed the third parameter `reserv_clstrs` from the function call to `ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used()` on line 6328.
intent_record.how: This change modifies the function invocation to pass only two arguments (ac and handle) instead of three. intent_record.intent_summary: Fix reserved cluster accounting by unconditionally releasing reserved clusters when they exist, rather than conditionally releasing them only on allocation failure without delalloc flag.
intent_record.what: Replaced a conditional block that checked `!ar->len` and `(ar->flags & EXT4_MB_DELALLOC_RESERVED) == 0` with a simpler condition that directly checks `if (reserv_clstrs)`. The percpu_counter_sub call now uses `reserv_clstrs` directly instead of the computed `inquota - ar->len` expression. Updated the comment from 'release all the reserved blocks if non delalloc' to 'release any reserved blocks'.
intent_record.how: This changes the logic for releasing reserved disk clusters. Previously, clusters were only released when allocation failed (`!ar->len`) AND the delalloc flag was not set. Now, clusters are released whenever `reserv_clstrs` is non-zero, regardless of allocation success or the delalloc flag. This simplifies the cleanup path and ensures reserved clusters are consistently released based on whether any were actually reserved, rather than on allocation outcome and flags.

relevance_review.reason: This group performs a refactoring to remove an unused parameter from the ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() function signature. While the vulnerability involves this function, the group's changes are purely API simplification and do not address the double decrement issue of the dirty clusters counter. The root cause requires fixing the error handling logic to prevent decrementing the counter twice, not removing unused parameters.

Group 1 directly addresses the double decrement vulnerability by removing the incorrect dirty cluster counter decrement in one of the two problematic code paths. Hunk 2 specifically targets the accounting inconsistency caused by the duplicate decrement, which is the core issue described in the root cause. Hunk 4 also fixes related reserved cluster accounting problems that stem from the same underlying issue with improper error handling during block allocation.
